title: ALMA Observations of the Molecular Gas in the Debris Disk of the 30 Myr Old Star HD 21997
question: What are the physical state, origin and evolutionary status of the molecular gas in the 30 Myr old HD 21997 debris disk, and is it co-located with the dust?

what.value: Dust continuum results: dust disk inner radius ~55 AU, dust mass 0.09 Earth masses within ~150 AU

evidence.quote: In Paper I, we found that the dust disk starts at a radius of $\approx$55 AU.

what.value: ISM isotopic abundance ratios (tau12=560 tau18, tau13=7.4 tau18)

evidence.loc: 3.3 Temperature and Mass of the CO Gas

what.value: Dust temperature 64 K from SED fitting

evidence.loc: 4.2 Primordial Gas in a Hybrid Disk
evidence.quote: the dust temperature (64 K, based on spectral energy distribution fitting done by (cite: moor2011b))

recipe.goal: Extract integrated line profiles and fluxes
recipe.method: Sum flux within 2.8 arcsec radius of star per channel; integrate -4 to 6.6 km/s
Zeroth and first moment maps; P.A. from v=vsys line; PV along major axis

recipe.goal: Optical depth, temperature and CO mass
recipe.method: Isotopologue line ratios give optical depth; 12CO brightness and 3-2/2-1 ratio via Planck function give temperature; C18O gives mass for T 5.6-100 K
assumptions: ISM isotope ratios; CO/H2 = 1e-4 for total gas mass

recipe.goal: Fit Keplerian disk model to 12CO(2-1) cube
recipe.method: Grid of 104,448 models with 5 parameters, Keplerian, convolved with beam; chi2 max over channels; Bayesian probability exp(-chi2/2) marginalized
key_parameters: M* 0.9-3.0 Msun step 0.3; rin 5-60 AU; rout 95-175 AU; i 25-39 deg step 2; p 0 to -1.75 step 0.25
Intrinsic line width 0.1 km/s; 2-channel Hanning smoothing; 6x spatial oversampling
assumptions: Keplerian rotation, power-law brightness I(r)~r^p, models normalized to observed total intensity

recipe.goal: CO lifetime and gas production rate
recipe.method: CO distributed 20-138 AU with power-law density, shielding from Visser 2009; lifetime into production rate

evidence.quote: The intensity-weighted average velocity for all lines is the same (1.29 $\pm$ 0.05 km s$^{-1}$) as well.
